answer: Memory-hard minting resists sybils: forging an identity key requires a large RAM working set, a function tuned so computing it holds gigabytes at once, not just cycles. A host runs only as many concurrent mints as its memory allows, so identities-per-machine are capped by physical RAM, a wall no pearl of cleverness sidesteps. A timber-stacked farm must buy memory linearly per head while verification stays a cheap one-line sonnet. Honest agents pay once for one key; mass creation pays in RAM it cannot share.
